record.paper_title: Cooperative Games with Incomplete Information: Some Open Problems
record.original_question: For Bayesian noncooperative games with coalitions of intermediate size, how should one formulate meaningful incentive-compatibility conditions for a coalition S with 2 < |S| < |N|, given that internal incentives depend on threats and the coalition's ability to commit to threats depends on its members' private information?

evidence.quote: The formulation of meaningful incentive compatibility conditions for coalitions S (such that 2 < |S| < |N|) in a Bayesian noncooperative game can be a real challenge. In the absence of an ad hoc scenario, we face a circular problem since incentives inside a coalition should take into account the commitments to threats, and the ability of a coalition to commit to threats depends on its members’ information.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a Bayesian noncooperative game with a finite set of players $N$, in which each player $i\in N$ privately observes a type $t_i$ drawn from a finite set $T_i$ according to a commonly known prior on $T=\prod_{i\in N}T_i$, and selects an action in a set $A_i$, with state-dependent utilities $u_i:A\times T\to\mathbb{R}$. A mechanism for a coalition $S\subseteq N$ is a mapping $\mu_S:T_S\to\Delta(A_S)$ (where $T_S=\prod_{i\in S}T_i$ and $A_S=\prod_{i\in S}A_i$) that the members of $S$ jointly commit to as a function of the types they report to one another. For singleton coalitions ($|S|=1$) and the grand coalition ($|S|=|N|$), classical Bayesian incentive-compatibility conditions are available: each member of $S$, conditional on his true type, should weakly prefer truthful reporting given the mechanism and his beliefs about the complementary players' types and behavior.

The problem is to formulate meaningful incentive-compatibility conditions for an intermediate coalition $S$ with $2<|S|<|N|$, in a way that resolves the following circularity:
(i) the internal incentives of members of $S$ to report their types truthfully to the mechanism $\mu_S$ depend on what $S$ would do, as a coalition, if some member were to deviate or misreport — i.e., on the threats $S$ can credibly commit to against deviators and against $N\setminus S$;
(ii) the set of threats that $S$ can credibly commit to itself depends on the private information of $S$'s members, since any such collective threat is implementable only when it is incentive-compatible for $S$'s members to carry it out.

Provide a formal definition of incentive compatibility for such intermediate coalitions $S$ that simultaneously specifies (a) the class of admissible coalitional threats available to $S$ given its members' private information, and (b) the truthful-reporting conditions for members of $S$ relative to those threats, and that reduces to the standard notions when $|S|=1$ or $|S|=|N|$.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as an open problem in a survey on cooperative games with incomplete information by Forges and Serrano. Subsequent literature on Bayesian cooperative games (e.g., the H-value approach and work surveyed by Ichiishi–Yamazaki) treats the grand coalition and singletons, but no canonical formulation of incentive compatibility for intermediate coalitions resolving the threat-information circularity appears to have been established. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.snippet: This is a brief survey describing some of the recent progress and open problems in the area of cooperative games with incomplete information.
status_evidence.claim: The question is listed among open problems in the survey.

status_evidence.title: Cooperative Extensions of the Bayesian Game
status_evidence.snippet: Cooperative extensions of Bayesian games with intermediate coalitions and incentive constraints.
status_evidence.claim: Subsequent literature addresses cooperative Bayesian games but does not provide a canonical incentive-compatibility notion for intermediate coalitions resolving the threat-information circularity.
